Phase 74a impl (test-only; no plan cycle, per the arbiter's rule for small fixes). docs/phases/launchpad-test-holds-the-fake-turn.md has the cause and evidence.

Flake: tests/test_launchpad.py::TestServerEndpoints::test_watch_session_and_launch_endpoints failed 3× on CI (main d49c632; PR #61 run 35960741817; PR #62 run 35963725788) with `assert conv["slot"]["held"]` false; the same code passed on re-run each time. Cause: the test's "still running" assertions relied on the fake turn lasting ~2 s (FAKE_AGENT_SLEEP=1.0); on a loaded runner the turn could end first, and lead_chat.run_turn releases the slot (finally) a few ms before finish_conversation_turn marks the row — a GET in that gap sees `running` + slot free. Demonstrated: with the sleep cut to 0.01 s the old test fails every time on its first "still running" assertion.

Fix (test-only; product code unchanged):
- tests/fixtures/fake_agent.py: FAKE_AGENT_HOLD=<path> — in chat mode, after the first event, wait until the file exists before replying (20 ms poll, 30 s cap so a broken test can't hang the suite). Unset → unchanged behaviour.
- tests/test_launchpad.py: the hold path is set before the launch; the file is created only at the completion section, so running / slot held / SSE line / pending-repeat are all asserted while the turn is provably held. The 1.0 s sleep override is gone (fixture's 0.05 s), so the test is ~2 s.
- Not changed, deliberately: the release-before-finish ordering in run_turn (a ms-wide, harmless product gap; reordering changes the slot lifecycle — out of scope for a test fix).

Verification: the test passes; 30/30 consecutive runs under load (4 busy loops on 8 cores) in 57 s. Full suite: the gate's run in this call.

Impl r2 — addresses the r1 GATE_BOUNCE (1 failed of 2,611: tests/test_jobs.py::TestLifecycle::test_fast_completion_keeps_the_runners_result — a second, unrelated test race of the same kind, from Phase 72).

Cause: `_wait_terminal` returned as soon as the job was terminal, but the runner adds `delivery` just after its commit (by design: at-most-once delivery recorded after the commit). The test's byte snapshot, taken between those two writes, differed at the sorted `delivery` key; the real-runner cancel test next to it read rec["delivery"] on the same timing.

Fix (test-only): `_wait_terminal` now returns when the job is terminal AND its runner has released runner.lock (`jobs.probe_runner(...) != "busy"`), then re-reads. Verified: tests/test_jobs.py 55 passed; the two real-runner tests 20/20 under load (4 busy loops / 8 cores). The launchpad fix from r1 is unchanged (30/30 under load). Phase doc + roadmap entry record both. Full suite: the gate's run in this call.

GATE: PASS | scope skipped | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2611 passed, 5 skipped, 9m09s)
